title: Will Democrats block Trump’s push to deliver Turkey F-35s, lift sanctions?
gist: Turkey is still pushing for F-35s and removal of CAATSA defense sanctions, betting on Trump and its NATO value, but the Nov. 2026 Democratic takeover of Congress complicates a path that runs through a statutory NDAA ban tied to Ankara's Russian S-400s.

insights.claim: Turkey is pressing to secure F-35 fighter jets and lift US defense sanctions, banking on President Donald Trump's support and its strategic NATO value despite Democratic midterm gains in Congress.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: A Trump-brokered Turkey deal would be a test of executive vs. Congressional power over arms sales.

insights.claim: Democratic control of Congress complicates Turkey's push for F-35s and sanctions relief, though Ankara remains hopeful Trump can still broker a deal.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Odds of F-35 delivery to Turkey fall with a Democratic Congress; watch NDAA language.
insights.quote: Ankara remains hopeful Trump can still broker a deal

insights.claim: In 2019 Washington halted Turkey's F-35 purchase over concerns that its Russian-made S-400 air defense system could collect intelligence on the stealth jets and compromise their technology; Ankara had paid roughly $1.7 billion for the jets.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: The $1.7bn already paid is a sunk-cost lever Ankara uses in negotiations.
insights.quote: Ankara had paid roughly $1.7 billion for the jets.

insights.claim: The fiscal 2020 National Defense Authorization Act prohibits F-35 transfers to Turkey until Ankara no longer possesses the Russian S-400 system, making the ban statutory rather than executive.
insights.speaker: Barin Kayaoglu
insights.so_what: Because the ban is in law, a Democratic Congress can block delivery regardless of Trump's wishes.
insights.quote: prohibits F-35 transfers to Turkey until Ankara no longer possesses the Russian system

insights.claim: The first Trump administration imposed CAATSA sanctions on Turkey's main defense procurement agency and four associated officials over the S-400 purchase.

insights.claim: Congress passed CAATSA in 2017 to deter third-country defense transactions with Iran, Russia and North Korea.
